title: Local smallness of a derived category with K-injective resolutions
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] whose Hom sets are equivalent to types in a universe $w$, and suppose $A$ has K-injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let $D(A)$ be any chosen derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with an arbitrary Hom universe. Then every Hom set of $D(A)$ is equivalent to a type in universe $w$.

proof.text: The category of cochain complexes is locally w-small, since a chain map is a countable family of maps satisfying equations. Its homotopy category is locally w-small because quotient Hom types remain small. The full subcategory of K-injectives is therefore locally w-small. HomotopyCategory.KInjectives.Qh is an equivalence when K-injective resolutions exist. Apply locallySmall_congr to this equivalence, exactly as in the existing proof of DerivedCategory.locallySmall.
